title: The Counting Loop (FOR)
objectives: Recognize the three parts of a counting loop (start, condition, step)
Write the right loop for a given range

hook.text: You need to print the numbers from 1 to 100 on the screen. Will you write 100 lines of the WRITE command?

concept.heading: The three parts of a loop
concept.body: Every counting loop has three pieces of information: where it starts, where it ends, and how much it increases each round.

concept.heading: Why does it work?
concept.body: A computer can do the same job thousands of times, but you only tell it once what to do. The loop takes over the repetition for you.

workedExamples.runnerSource:
FOR i ← 1 TO 5 STEP 1
  WRITE i
END_LOOP

steps.explain: The variable i takes the value 1.
i becomes 2 (the loop continues because it has not passed 5).

exercises.question: How many times does the loop FOR i ← 3 TO 7 STEP 1 run?

feedback.correct: Correct. 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 makes 5 rounds. The range includes both ends.
feedback.incorrect: Count both ends: from 3 to 7 there are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. (7 - 3) + 1 = 5.

exercises.hint: In each round, add i to total.

exercises.question: What does this algorithm print on the screen?
exercises.hint: The step is 2, so the counter goes up by 2 each round.

exercises.question: Complete the loop that prints the numbers from 1 to 10.
Put the steps of the algorithm that adds the numbers from 1 to 3 in the correct order.
What happens if you change the counter variable by hand inside the body of a counting loop?
options: It becomes unpredictable how many times the loop will run
The program gives an error and stops

feedback.correct: Correct. Changing the counter by hand breaks the flow of the loop and leads to unexpected results.
feedback.incorrect: The counter is under the loop's own control; changing it by hand makes it unpredictable how many rounds will run.

summary: Counting loop: start, end condition, step.
Changing the counter variable by hand inside the loop causes mistakes.
